title: Persistence diagnostics: split COMMIT into WAL write / fsync / checkpoint and retain the slowest recent ticks
outcome: Persistence diagnostics: split COMMIT into WAL write / fsync / checkpoint and retain the slowest recent ticks
acceptance: /api/diagnostics/persistence reports, for each writer tick, the time spent inside the SQLite COMMIT call separately from surrounding transaction and cleanup work; where obtainable without changing checkpoint behaviour (e.g. a behaviour-equivalent WAL hook that reproduces SQLite's default PASSIVE autocheckpoint at the configured threshold, proven by a test), it also reports the WAL frame count after commit and any autocheckpoint duration; any sub-phase that cannot be measured honestly is reported as unavailable, never as zero. Persisted data and format are unchanged.
The endpoint retains the N slowest ticks seen since start (or within a bounded window) in addition to the last 16, so a 20-30 s spike remains inspectable minutes later; bounded memory.
Focused tests cover the new fields and the slowest-tick retention; existing persistence tests pass on the exact input.
